newsitem.title: USA: Kansas wheat condition improves with rains.
newsitem.headline: Kansas wheat condition improves with rains.

text.p: Kansas winter wheat condition improved during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop progress report.

Wheat condition was rated 13 percent excellent, 53 good, 23 fair, eight poor and three percent very poor. That compared to the previous week's rating of 11 percent excellent, 49 good, 29 fair, nine poor and two percent very poor.
Sixty percent of the wheat was turning color, well ahead of 46 percent last year and the five-year average of 47 percent.
Sorghum was 65 percent planted, ahead of 59 percent last year and the average of 47 percent. Soybeans were 80 percent seeded, ahead of 61 last year the average of 52 percent.

Corn condition also improved and was rated 14 percent excellent, 65 good, 18 fair, two poor and three percent very poor. That compared to the previous week's rating of 10 percent excellent, 71 percent good, 18 percent fair, one percent poor and nil very poor.
Pasture condition was rated 11 percent excellent, 65 good, 19 fair and five percent poor.
